title: Gabriel’s Bagels: Atlanta’s best new bagel, six years in the making
summary: After six years of baking at home, Gabriel launched Gabriel’s Bagels in Atlanta through weekend pop-ups, Hotplate drops, and local coffee shop partnerships.
body_text: 📍 Atlanta, GA 🔗 hotplate.com/gabrielsbagels Gabriel had been baking bagels at home for six years before he ever sold one. Just a few weeks ago, he hosted his first pop-up and sold 52 bagels. He’s already sold over 100 for his upcoming third drop. “It was a long time coming,” he says. “But about a month ago, I just decided - I’m going to start doing this. The ball just started rolling and getting bigger and bigger and bigger and all this crazy stuff is happening.” How it started Gabriel’s been baking for a long time, experimenting with pizza, bread, croissants, cinnamon rolls, donuts, and more. Bagels were what stuck. They were what he felt most confident in and enjoyed most. “Bagels are both what I felt I'm best at, can be consistent at, and what I love to eat all the time. I eat way too many bagels. And so the last couple of years, that's what I've been really trying to perfect.” Even so, starting a real operation and actually selling felt like a big step. He went back and forth on this for years. What finally convinced him was seeing other bagel bakers on social media. “I'm scrolling reels a month or so ago. And I see people doing it…And they're being successful with what they're doing.” Watching other entrepreneurs “just owning it and doing it” was the turning point for Gabriel. It led to the realization that: “If they can do it, I can do it because I know what I’m able to bake. It just all just happened after that. I got a rush of that motivation and just went with it and took it and it's still going.” Getting his first customers Before he posted his first drop on Hotplate, Gabriel wanted to see if people would even be interested. He tried something simple to test the waters. A week before his first drop, he scaled up his normal recipe for 12 bagels to 60, and took the best 45 to a local farmers market. “I set up a table on the street leading into the market and handed out samples,” he says. He also had also printed out his Hotplate SMS QR code, making it easy for people to subscribe after sampling. A week later, he got two orders from friends, and seven from strangers who had stopped by for samples. From that one morning outside the farmer’s market, he attracted genuine fans, some of whom have ordered every drop since. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Gabriel’s Bagels (@gabrielsbagels) What his bagel business looks like today Right now, Gabriel is hand rolling, boiling, and freshly baking his bagels alongside his full-time job in data consulting. He keeps his schedule focused and manageable to balance both. He preps on Friday and bakes Sunday morning ahead of pickups. He dedicates a few hours throughout the week to other tasks like planning and getting ready for the next drop. Things have started to pick up quickly, especially through word of mouth in the Atlanta food community. When we spoke to Gabriel last week, he was waiting on a Costco delivery for an extra refrigerator so he could proof more bagels at once. He’s also upgrading to a larger convection oven as demand continues to grow. “It used to be making them for myself once a week…But now it’s like, I have to do it three times through this weekend for people who are giving me money to do it. Like it doesn’t feel real.” He’s also starting to expand beyond direct-to-customer drops. He brought his bagels to a local coffee shop for the owner to try. “He texted me over the weekend…He wanted to drop his factory bagel supplier for me. He gave away samples as well and he said people were floored by them.” Looking ahead Gabriel might just be starting out, but he has hard-earned momentum and goals. Long term, he’d love to open up his own shop but for now, he’s focused on building something steady through pop-ups, preorders, and local partnerships. Like many microbakers, he’s also learning from others in the space, especially Barrett’s Bagels in Madison, WI, who shares advice about not expanding too quickly. That perspective has helped him stay patient and focus on getting the fundamentals right first. Right now, the goal is to keep improving, keep showing up each week, and keep building a loyal customer base. Keep crushing it, Gabriel! Your Hotplate team is rooting for you!

title: Activator: A Tool or a Technique?
summary: Discover why chiropractors use the activator, an FDA-approved tool for gentle, precise, and effective chiropractic adjustments supporting spinal health.
body_text: The Activator Method is a widely used, research-informed chiropractic technique that offers a precise, low-force alternative to traditional manual adjustments. Instead of using hands to apply pressure, chiropractors use a small, spring-loaded tool to deliver quick, targeted impulses to the spine or joints. This method avoids the "popping" or “cracking” sound common with other techniques and offers a gentle, consistent, and effective approach to care for many people. Developed decades ago and receiving FDA approval in 1997, the Activator Method is one of the most researched low-force chiropractic techniques available. If you're new to chiropractic care or seeking a gentler adjustment, the Activator Method provides a well-established and trusted option. What is the Activator Method in chiropractic care? The Activator Method chiropractic technique is a clinical approach that uses both a specialized instrument and a detailed assessment protocol to guide spinal adjustments. The method was developed to offer an alternative to traditional manual adjustments. Instead of twisting or manipulating the spine by hand, chiropractors use a handheld instrument called the activator to deliver quick, controlled impulses to specific points on the body. The goal is to restore joint motion, reduce muscular tension, and improve nervous system function through precise, low-force corrections. The Activator Method combines detailed analysis with repeatable mechanics, ensuring a consistent and measurable adjustment experience. What is the difference between the activator chiropractic tool and the Activator Method? When people hear the term “activator” in chiropractic care, they’re often referring to both the tool and the technique. While the two are closely connected, they are not the same. The tool: The activator adjusting instrument is a handheld, spring-loaded device that delivers a quick, low-force mechanical impulse to a specific joint throughout the body.. It’s engineered for precision, offering a controlled adjustment with minimal joint movement. For many patients, the sensation is subtle, often described as a light tap. The method: The Activator Method is the clinical protocol behind the tool’s use. Chiropractors trained in this technique follow a detailed sequence of assessments to identify areas of dysfunction. These evaluations include biomechanical tests, leg length analysis, and neurological checks, all of which guide the placement and application of the activator. Together, the tool and the method form a complete system. The activator delivers the adjustment. The method ensures it’s delivered to the right place, in the right way, at the right time. This combination creates a repeatable, science-informed approach that emphasizes precision, consistency, and patient comfort, setting it apart from traditional manual techniques. How does the Activator Method work? The activator works by delivering a fast, localized mechanical impulse to a specific joint or vertebra. This quick thrust stimulates the surrounding soft tissues and spinal nerves, which may help restore joint motion, ease muscle tension, and support nervous system function. Here’s what the activator method looks like in practice: The chiropractor begins with a biomechanical assessment to identify areas of dysfunction, such as joint restrictions, muscular imbalances, or altered reflexes. Once the area is identified, the activator delivers a quick, targeted thrust to the precise location that needs adjustment. The device’s speed allows the adjustment to occur before surrounding muscles can contract or resist, creating a smooth, low-force correction without joint twisting or cracking. What makes this technique unique is its ability to blend speed and control. Because the activator is engineered to deliver a consistent force, it provides chiropractors with an effective way to adjust a single vertebra or joint without affecting nearby tissues. This combination of precision, comfort, and consistency is what makes the Activator Method a powerful alternative to traditional manual adjustments. Why chiropractors use the Activator Method for adjustments? Every person’s spine and nervous system are unique. That’s why chiropractors often choose the activator when a patient’s condition, comfort level, or anatomy calls for a gentle, controlled approach. Here are several reasons chiropractors may choose the Activator Method: Gentle care: The low-force impulse is ideal for individuals who are sensitive to manual adjustments or nervous about the noise often associated with manual adjustments. Consistent results: The instrument provides a uniform thrust each time, helping to maintain consistency from visit to visit. High precision: The narrow application area enables detailed adjustments in the upper cervical spine, ribs, wrists, or other small joints. Patient reassurance: For individuals who are anxious about twisting or cracking sounds, the activator provides a calming alternative. We believe chiropractic care should meet you where you are. That means selecting the method that works best for your body and your preferences. The activator helps us do that with both precision and flexibility. Who benefits most from the Activator Method of chiropractic care? Not everyone responds to chiropractic care in the same way. Some people feel their best after a hands-on, manual adjustment. Others benefit more from a gentler, instrument-assisted approach. That’s where the Activator Method may come in. So, how do you know if you’re a good candidate? The answer depends on your health history, comfort level, preferences, and treatment goals. The Activator Method is designed to offer a low-force, highly controlled adjustment. That makes it an excellent option for a wide range of individuals who need or prefer a more gentle approach. You may be a strong candidate for the Activator Method if: You're new to chiropractic care: If this is your first experience with adjustments, you may feel more comfortable starting with a gentle, non-manual technique. You prefer a quiet approach: Some people would rather avoid the popping or cracking often associated with manual adjustments. You prefer a gentler approach: Some people feel that too much force is applied during a manual adjustment. If that is the case, the Activator Method is an excellent option. You're managing a specific condition: If you have arthritis, osteoporosis, fibromyalgia, or another condition that makes your joints or tissues more sensitive, the Activator Method offers a conservative and safe alternative. You're recovering from an injury: After trauma or surgery, it's essential to avoid forceful manipulation. The precision of the activator allows chiropractors to adjust specific joints without straining surrounding areas. You're a child or older adult: The Activator Method is often ideal for younger or older patients who may need a more delicate technique tailored to their unique anatomy and developmental stage. You’ve had previous spinal surgery or structural changes: When anatomy has been altered due to surgery, degeneration, or congenital differences, a tool-based approach offers greater control and customization. Even if none of these situations apply, the Activator Method can still be a great option for anyone seeking a more targeted and consistent adjustment. Chiropractors use this method because it allows them to meet your body where it is, providing care that’s both effective and comfortable. To ensure your chiropractor can choose the most appropriate techniques, you must share your full medical history and communicate any conditions, past surgeries, or concerns before beginning care. This helps your doctor of chiropractic make the best decisions for your safety, comfort, and results. Before making any adjustments, your chiropractor will take the time to understand your needs, assess your spine, and explain the approach they recommend. Suppose the Activator Method is part of your personalized plan. In that case, you can feel confident it was chosen for a reason: because it may help support your mobility, reduce discomfort, and move you closer to feeling your best. Do all chiropractors use the Activator Method? Not every chiropractor uses the activator or practices the Activator Method. Like any clinical technique, this method requires specific training and certification. Chiropractors who choose to use it do so because they believe it serves a purpose within personalized, evidence-informed care. At The Joint Chiropractic, we always begin by listening to your concerns and evaluating your body. If we recommend the activator, it’s because we believe it aligns with your specific needs and comfort level. If you are curious about whether you would benefit from being adjusted by an activator or want to know if it is available at your local clinic, simply ask during your visit. You always deserve to understand your care. We’re here to guide you through every choice and ensure you feel confident in the method we recommend. Is the Activator Method safe? The Activator Method is recognized as a safe and effective technique within the chiropractic profession. It is widely used in both private practice and teaching clinics and has been reviewed in numerous clinical studies. In 1997, the activator received FDA approval as a regulated medical device. Because the activator delivers force in a controlled, low-intensity way, it avoids many of the risks associated with more forceful manual manipulations. The quick, precise movement limits joint rotation and protects nearby tissues. Key safety advantages: Calibrated force delivery: The tool is engineered to deliver a precise impulse based on standardized tension settings. Minimal joint movement: This helps reduce the risk of overcorrection or soft tissue strain. Repeatable accuracy: Each adjustment can be delivered in the same way, helping chiropractors monitor progress and outcomes Chiropractors are trained to assess whether this method is appropriate for each person and to adapt their approach as needed. If you have questions or concerns about safety, we welcome the opportunity to talk you through how the activator works and how we use it. Is the Activator Method effective for spinal adjustments? The Activator Method is one of the most researched and widely used instrument-assisted techniques in chiropractic care. It may be just as effective as manual adjustments for many people and is especially helpful for those seeking a more focused, lower-force option. Here is what the research about the activator method shows: Systematic review of eight clinical trials A study published in The Journal of the Canadian Chiropractic Association evaluated outcomes from eight clinical trials involving the Activator Adjusting Instrument and compared its effectiveness against that of manual adjustments. The review concluded that instrument-assisted adjustments were as effective as manual adjustments in reducing spinal pain, addressing temporomandibular joint dysfunction, and relieving trigger point discomfort in the trapezius muscle. Improvements in neuromuscular function Additional research published in The Journal of Manipulative and Physiological Therapeutics found that activator adjustments may influence muscle activity and spinal joint motion. These neuromechanical effects support the Activator Method’s role in promoting functional movement and spinal health. Ongoing use in diverse care plans The Activator Method is routinely integrated into chiropractic care plans for individuals experiencing neck pain, low back discomfort, restricted mobility, or joint stiffness. Its precise, low-force delivery makes it a valuable tool for addressing spinal dysfunction without the need for high-velocity manual thrusts. While outcomes vary based on each person’s health history and response to care, the research supports the Activator Method as a safe, reliable, and clinically appropriate approach that may help reduce pain, improve mobility, and support nervous system balance. What to know before your first activator adjustment If you are considering chiropractic care using the activator, there are a few things to know before your first visit: The tool makes a clicking sound but usually causes no discomfort. Adjustments are often so gentle that you may barely feel them. Your chiropractor will likely assess leg length, reflex response, and joint motion to determine where to adjust. You can ask questions at any time and request a different method if you prefer. We believe your care should feel collaborative, informed, and comfortable. Whether you’re curious about the activator or simply seeking a new chiropractic approach, we’re here to help. Why the Activator Method may be the right choice for your chiropractic care The Activator Method provides a trusted and well-studied alternative to traditional chiropractic adjustments. By using a handheld device to deliver fast, controlled impulses, chiropractors can support better alignment, mobility, and nervous system function in a way that feels gentle and targeted. At The Joint Chiropractic, we know every body is different. That’s why we take the time to evaluate your needs and recommend the method that fits your goals. The activator is one of the tools we may use to help you feel better, move better, and live better. All without appointments, insurance, or pressure. body_text: The way we create, manage, and deliver content is changing fast. Two technologies are leading that charge: headless CMS architecture and AI agents. On their own, each is powerful. Together, they're transforming how teams build digital experiences. Let's break down why this combination matters and how you can start taking advantage of it today. Note: This article was written using Kimi K3 , Moonshot AI's open-source frontier model. Kimi K3 will be available as a built-in model inside Cosmic soon... stay tuned What Is a Headless CMS? (A Quick Refresher) A traditional CMS bundles your content backend with a specific frontend. Think of the classic monolithic website platforms. A headless CMS removes that constraint by separating content management from presentation entirely. Your content lives in a central hub and is delivered via APIs to anywhere: Websites and web apps Mobile applications Smart devices and wearables Digital signage and kiosks AI agents This API-first approach means your content is future-proof. A new channel emerges? You don't rebuild anything. You just connect. What Are AI Agents? AI agents go beyond simple chatbots or one-off prompts. An AI agent is a system that can perceive, reason, and act, often autonomously, to accomplish goals. Think of agents that can: Research topics and draft content briefs Generate and optimize copy for different channels Analyze performance data and suggest improvements Automate repetitive publishing workflows Personalize content for different audience segments The key difference from basic AI tools: agents don't just respond. They do things . They chain tasks together, make decisions, and interact with other systems through APIs. Why Headless CMS + AI Agents Work So Well Together AI agents need structured, accessible data to work with. A headless CMS provides exactly that. 1. Structured Content Is Agent-Friendly Content AI agents thrive on structure. When your content is stored as well-defined objects with clear fields, types, and relationships, agents can read, write, and manipulate it programmatically. No scraping messy HTML. No guessing at page layouts. Just clean, predictable data. 2. APIs Are the Perfect Handshake Because headless CMS platforms expose content through APIs, AI agents can plug in directly: Your agent becomes a first-class citizen in your content workflow, drafting, updating, localizing, and organizing content alongside your human team. 3. Automation That Actually Scales Imagine an agent that: Monitors your analytics for underperforming pages Rewrites headlines and meta descriptions for better SEO Creates localized versions for your international markets Submits everything as drafts for human review With a headless CMS, this workflow is an afternoon of API integration, not a months-long engineering project. 4. Humans Stay in Control The best part of this pairing: the CMS remains your single source of truth with built-in guardrails. Revision history, draft states, role-based permissions, and approval workflows mean AI agents accelerate your team without going rogue. Humans review, refine, and publish. Agents handle the heavy lifting. Pick a high-volume, low-risk task like generating meta descriptions or alt text. Use API keys with scoped permissions. Give agents exactly the access they need, no more. Keep humans in the loop. Route agent output to drafts first. Build trust, then expand autonomy. Measure and iterate. Track time saved, content quality, and engagement. Let data guide your next automation. Una delle principali sfide che Polytag si trova ad affrontare è il tracciamento e la raccolta di dati relativi alle plastiche monouso. Sebbene possa sembrare un processo semplice, in realtà è estremamente complesso: le plastiche differiscono notevolmente per forma, colore e dimensione, e spesso vengono mescolate o compresse all’interno dei flussi di riciclo. Per indirizzare questa sfida, le aziende applicano marcatori UV 2D invisibili sulle etichette dei propri imballaggi. Questi vengono poi rilevati tramite le unità di rilevamento Polytag, consentendo l’identificazione in tempo reale dell’origine dei materiali, dei tassi di riciclo e della destinazione a fine vita. Grazie a Aurora Vision Library di Zebra, il sistema elabora con precisione 20 fotogrammi al secondo, riuscendo a leggere codici 2D anche su nastri trasportatori ad alta velocità e in condizioni di scarsa illuminazione. “La nostra missione è fornire alle organizzazioni gli strumenti necessari per prendere decisioni più intelligenti e basate sui dati in tema di sostenibilità,” ha dichiarato Jonathan Anderson, Chief Technology Officer di Polytag. “Grazie all’integrazione della soluzione di Zebra, abbiamo raggiunto un livello di precisione senza precedenti nel tracciamento dei rifiuti, rendendo la piena circolarità un obiettivo concretamente raggiungibile.” Precisione, affidabilità e scalabilità grazie alla machine vision Inizialmente, Polytag utilizzava sistemi di telecamere embedded per la fase di proof of concept, ma questo approccio non garantiva la scalabilità necessaria per le operazioni industriali. Alla ricerca di una soluzione più solida, Polytag ha collaborato con Zebra e Automatica, partner Zebra per l’automazione industriale, riducendo sensibilmente i costi, oltre a migliorare l’affidabilità e la scalabilità del sistema. “Aurora Vision Library ha offerto un’integrazione perfetta con i nostri sistemi, permettendo la raccolta di dati approfonditi in tempo reale,” ha aggiunto Anderson. “Stiamo trasformando i centri di riciclo, adottando operazioni intelligenti che accelerano i flussi di lavoro e forniscono insight immediatamente utilizzabili.” Il sistema Polytag abilita letture accurate in tutti i centri di riciclo, anche su linee ad alta velocità, senza la necessità di modificare l’hardware di visione esistente. Il software Aurora è inoltre in gradi di operare con hardware di terze parti, offrendo agli utenti maggiore flessibilità e compatibilità retroattiva. Anche in condizioni difficili – come ambienti umidi, polverosi o scarsamente illuminati – gli operatori in prima linea possono tracciare con precisione i rifiuti grazie a questa soluzione. Le dashboard in tempo reale consentono alle organizzazioni di monitorare le performance di riciclo per SKU e per area geografica, individuando schemi ricorrenti e identificando prodotti con tassi di recupero inferiori, come bibite acquistate durante gli spostamenti o flaconi di shampoo utilizzati negli hotel. Queste informazioni permettono di sviluppare campagne di riciclo mirate e strategie di design più efficaci in grado di orientare le scelte dei consumatori verso comportamenti più sostenibili. “Vogliamo promuovere un cambiamento sistemico,” ha affermato Anderson. “In questo modo le aziende possono prendere decisioni più consapevoli basandosi su ciò che accade ai loro imballaggi nel mondo reale, non solo sui materiali di cui sono composti. La soluzione Zebra è stata fondamentale per trasformare questa visione in una realtà operativa.” Raggiungere tassi di rilevamento del 100% La soluzione di Polytag sta già generando un impatto significativo sull’intero ecosistema del riciclo. Con l’evoluzione delle normative sulla Responsabilità Estesa del Produttore (EPR) che richiedono sempre più dati precisi relativi ai rifiuti da imballaggio, la piattaforma “describe, tag and trace” di Polytag offre una visibilità senza precedenti sul ciclo di vita del riciclo. “Durante la fase di ricerca e sviluppo, abbiamo installato sei unità in un impianto progettato appositamente per testare e ottimizzare le nuove tecnologie di riciclo in condizioni reali,” ha spiegato Anderson. “Grazie alle scansioni ad alta fedeltà di Zebra, gestite tramite la piattaforma Aurora, siamo riusciti a raggiungere un tasso di rilevamento senza precedenti del 100%.” Questo risultato consente alle organizzazioni di soddisfare più facilmente i requisiti imposti dalla normativa EPR. L’obiettivo è chiaro: passare da stime e ipotesi a dati reali, che mostrano con chiarezza quali prodotti vengono effettivamente riciclati e quali no. “Il successo di Polytag rappresenta una chiara testimonianza del potere della visibilità degli asset e dell’automazione intelligente abilitata dal software,” ha commentato Donato Montanari, Vice President e General Manager, Machine Vision, Zebra Technologies. “Insieme stiamo affrontando una sfida concreta, ripensando il modo in cui il mondo gestisce i rifiuti e creando nuovi modelli operativi che migliorano la vita quotidiana delle organizzazioni, dei loro dipendenti e delle persone che servono.” PUNTI CHIAVE Grazie a Aurora Vision Library di Zebra, Polytag ha raggiunto una precisione del 100% nel rilevamento e tracciamento degli imballaggi, trasformando le operazioni di riciclo grazie ai dati in tempo reale. L’integrazione degli strumenti di visione di Zebra riduce i costi e consente a Polytag di implementare sistemi di tracciamento dei rifiuti scalabili e affidabili. La soluzione fornisce insight concreti, aiutando le organizzazioni a rispettare le normative EPR e a promuovere pratiche di packaging sostenibile.
